slides.title: Day 2 — First AI Code Goes Live
slides.subtitle: Authentication. The thing your client cares about most.
slides.opening_hook: Auth is where most AI builds fall apart. The prompt has to be tight or you ship a security hole.
bullets: Auth = the first feature on Day 2. Why? Because every other feature needs it.
We use JWT — token-based auth. Industry standard. Works for SPAs.
The auth prompt MUST hit all 8 components (remember Module 3's intent anatomy).
Today we show you the actual prompt that produced our Issue Tracker's auth — and what AI got wrong on first try.
slides.closing_thread: Here's the prompt that went into the AI tool.

slides.title: The Auth Prompt — All 8 Components
slides.subtitle: Real prompt · from the Issue Tracker engagement

hero_stat.label: intent components present — outcome, actor, validation, security, stack, acceptance, edge cases, data model

analogy.title: A locksmith's spec sheet
analogy.text: You don't tell a locksmith 'make me a door'. You tell them: width, swing, lock type, key cuts, fire rating, frame material. That's an auth prompt — every dimension explicit, or the door's wrong.

bullets: OUTCOME: Users with email + password can log in; protected routes require a valid JWT.
ACTOR: Admin, Manager, Reporter — three roles with different menu access.
VALIDATION: Email format, password ≥ 8 chars with mixed case, account-locked after 5 failed attempts.
SECURITY: Bcrypt hash (cost 12), JWT with 24h expiry, refresh tokens, server-side guards on EVERY protected route.
STACK: NestJS @nestjs/jwt + Passport, Prisma User model, React Context for auth state.
ACCEPTANCE: Valid login → 200 + token, invalid → 401, token expired → 401 with redirect to /login.
EDGE CASES: Empty fields, malformed email, brute force, expired token mid-action.
DATA MODEL: User { id, email UNIQUE, passwordHash, role ENUM, createdAt, lastLoginAt }.
slides.memory_hook: Eight components. Each one closes an ambiguity that AI would otherwise resolve with assumptions.
slides.closing_thread: What did AI generate? And what did we need to re-prompt?

slides.title: Manual Validation — You Test Auth Yourself
slides.subtitle: Don't trust the AI's word — run it, click it, watch the network tab.
bullets: Step 1: npm run start:dev — backend up. Visit localhost:3000/auth/login in browser, see 401.
Step 2: npm run dev — frontend up. Visit localhost:5173, see login page.
Step 3: Try a wrong password — should see error toast. Open browser dev tools → Network tab. Confirm 401 response.
Step 4: Try correct admin login — should redirect to dashboard. Confirm JWT in localStorage.
Step 5: Try hitting /api/issues with no token (use curl or Postman). Should see 401. Server-side guard works.
All 5 green? Auth is solid. If any fails — re-prompt with the specific error message.
slides.memory_hook: 5-step manual smoke test. Takes 5 minutes. You can't skip this and call it done.
slides.closing_thread: Auth shipped. Now the shell that wraps every other screen.

slides.title: The Re-Prompt That Fixed the N+1
slides.subtitle: Surgical, 2 sentences, references the exact file
bullets: Bad re-prompt: 'fix performance' — vague, AI guesses. Don't do this.
Good re-prompt: 'In dashboard.service.ts, getDashboardMetrics() is making 4 separate Prisma calls. Combine into 1 query using groupBy + raw aggregations.'
AI returns: a single Prisma $queryRaw with COUNT/SUM groupings, drops query count from 4 → 1.
Add: 'Also add @@index([assigneeId, status]) and @@index([dueDate]) to schema.prisma.' Two re-prompts. Done.
Total dashboard time including re-prompts: ~90 minutes. From zero to shipped + indexed.
slides.memory_hook: Re-prompts are SURGICAL. Name the file. Name the function. Name the gap. Reference the fix shape.
slides.closing_thread: Auth, shell, dashboard — all live. Time for YOU to see it.
slides.narration: The re-prompt that fixed the N-plus-one. Bad — fix performance, vague. Good — name the file, name the function, name the gap, suggest the shape of the fix. Two re-prompts, ninety minutes total, dashboard ships indexed.

slides.title: Spot the gaps in this auth prompt
slides.subtitle: Click each clause that breaks the 8-component rule
slides.text: Add login to the app. Use JWT. Make sure the password is secure. Roles are admin and user. Block bad logins.

flaws.phrase: Make sure the password is secure
flaws.explanation: Vague. Secure how? Bcrypt cost? Argon2? Length minimum? Complexity rules? Without a specific algorithm and cost, AI picks SHA-256 and ships a CVE-ready system.
Two roles only? The FDD says three — Admin, Manager, Reporter. AND missing the action map — who can do WHAT. Roles without permission scope = useless.
After how many? With what cool-down? Account lockout? Captcha? IP throttle? 'Bad' has zero shape — AI ships a token check and calls it done.
